title: Protocol for optimizing production and quality control of infective EcoHIV virions
protocol: Make 500 mL of LB media.
Add 7.5 g agar to the LB media.
Autoclave on liquid small cycle (20 min exposure).
Let the agar cool until it is warm but not hot to touch.
Add ampicillin (100 μg/mL, final) to the cooled mixture.
Pour approximately 25 mL of the mixture into plates.
Let plates sit capped to solidify.
Cap the plates and store at 4°C until use.
Clean the lab bench with 70% ethanol.
Set the water bath at 42°C.
Thaw a 50 μL aliquot of DH5α E. coli on ice.
Add 1 μL of plasmid to the DH5α E. coli and keep it on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the bacteria at 42°C for 1.5 min.
Keep the cells on ice for 2 min.
Add the bacteria to the agar plate and spread them.
Incubate the plate upside down at 37°C overnight (maximum for 16 h).
Pick one colony and add it to 4 mL autoclaved LB media supplemented with 100 μg/mL ampicillin in a sterile culture tube.
Incubate the culture at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm for 8 h.
Transfer 4 mL of the LB media containing the colony into 1 L autoclaved LB media with 100 μg/mL ampicillin and shake at 250 rpm at 37°C overnight.
Harvest the bacteria by centrifugation at 3,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Measure the plasmid concentration using Nanodrop.
Check the integrity and quality of EcoHIV plasmids before proceeding with EcoHIV production.
Perform a diagnostic restriction digest using Hind III on EcoHIV-NDK to generate 6 fragments.
Observe the fragments sized at 1086, 1172, 1786, 2686, 3235 and 5353 bp for EcoHIV-NDK.
Perform a diagnostic restriction digest using Hind III on EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP to generate 7 fragments.
Observe the fragments sized at 1086, 1172, 1308, 1786, 2686, 3235 and 5353 bp for EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP.
Prepare a 1% agarose gel.
Add 100 mL of 1 X TBE buffer into an Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 1 g agarose to the Erlenmeyer flask.
Microwave the mixture for 55 s to melt the agarose.
Swirl the Erlenmeyer flask to mix the agarose.
Microwave again for 15 s.
Add 6 μL Ethidium Bromide and mix well.
Pour the solution into the Owl™ EasyCast™ B2 Mini Gel Electrophoresis Systems.
Insert the appropriate gel comb.
Let the solution set to solidify at room temperature.
Label two Eppendorf tubes as (cut) and (no cut).
Add 16 μL distilled H2O to each tube.
Add 2 μL of smart cut 10 X buffer to each tube.
Add 1 μL of plasmid of interest (160 ng/μL) to each tube.
Add 1 μL of Hind III-HF to the "cut" tube and 1 μL distilled H2O to the "uncut" tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 1.5 h.
Add 2.2 μL of 10 X DNA loading dye.
Load 10 μL into the 1% agarose gel.
Run the gel at 120 V for 1.5 h using 1 x TBE as the running buffer.
Image the gel using Ethidium Bromide filter with the ChemiDoc imaging system.
Plate 6×10^6 Lenti-X™ 293T cells in a 150 mm × 20 mm tissue culture treated dish in 20 mL growing media without antibiotics.
Ensure cell viability is >85% to achieve good viral titers.
Ensure cells are 60–70% confluent before transfection.
Prepare 12 mL of DMEM for each plate.
Add 18 μL of 40,000 PEI MAX (linear) stock concentration: 5 mg/mL to the DMEM.
Add 30 μg of EcoHIV plasmid to the solution.
Vortex the mixture for 1 minute.
Mix by inversion for 1 hour at room temperature.
Remove media from plates with a sterile pipet.
Add transfection media dropwise against the side wall of the dish.
After 6 hours, add 13 mL of growing media without antibiotics in a dropwise manner to the plate.
Incubate cells for 24 hours and add 20 mL of growing media without antibiotics.
Collect supernatant after 24 hours.
Spin supernatant at 3,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Store the supernatant for viral concentration at 4°C.
Place SW28 rotor in the ultracentrifuge and cool it to 4°C before starting the run.
Add up to 35 mL of media from infected cells into ultra-clear centrifuge tubes.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.2 μm filtration unit (optional).
Use a sucrose pad (20% sucrose) or a sucrose gradient (20–70% sucrose) and add the filtered supernatant as described in step b.
Add the supernatant slowly on top of sucrose to prevent mixing the layers together.
Ensure proper balancing of the tubes.
Spin at 35,300 × g with acceleration and brake set to 7 for 3 hours.
Discard media via aspiration or quick dumping into a waste container with bleach after centrifugation.
Add 350 μL of cold PBS to each tube and swirl gently to resuspend the virus pellet.
Place the tubes on a rocker at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Pool collected virus suspensions together and mix well by rocking again at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Aliquot the virus preparations (100 μL) into cryogenic vials.
Avoid introducing air bubbles during suspension to keep viral particles intact.
Snap-freeze the tubes in a methanol/dry ice bath or with liquid nitrogen.
Store the tubes at -80°C.
Calculate the virus titer using an aliquot that has been subjected to one freeze/thaw cycle.
Ensure EcoHIV can tolerate only one freeze/thaw cycle.
Prepare a 40% PEG-8000 solution in a biological safety cabinet (1.2 M NaCl in PBS pH 7.4).
Filter sterilize the prepared PEG-8000 solution.
Mix the collected supernatant from the 3,000 × g spin with the PEG-8000 solution at a ratio of 4:1 (20 mL supernatant to 5 mL PEG solution).
Incubate the mixture overnight at 4°C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,500 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Spin the pellet tube again at 1,500 × g for 1 minute at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL sterile PBS if the starting volume was 20 mL media (resulting in a 100-fold concentration).
Do not use polystyrene tubes to store the virus; use cryogenic vials instead.
Avoid introducing air bubbles while suspending the viral pellet to maintain integrity of viral particles.
Evaluate infectivity and quality of newly made virus preparations using HEK293-mCAT1 cells, provided by Dr. Alan Rein, NIH/NCI.
Utilize EcoHIV versions expressing EGFP (EcoHIV-EGFP NL4/3 or EcoHIV-EGFP NDK) for the infectivity assay.
Split HEK293-mCAT1 cells into a 24-well plate (plate A) with 1 × 10^5 cells/well in 1 mL final volume for next-day infection.
Add 450 μL of growing media to each well in a fresh 24-well plate (plate B).
Mix 50 μL virus with the first well of plate B thoroughly, then serially transfer 50 μL into remaining wells of plate B for 10-fold dilutions.
Aspirate and discard the media from plate A.
Transfer 400 μL from the first well of plate B to the first well of plate A, then continue transferring media from other wells of plate B to plate A.
Include a non-infected cell control to determine background.
Incubate cells for 24–48 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Aspirate the media from the HEK293-mCAT1 cells after incubation.
Add 100 μL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA to the cells and incubate for 5 min.
Add 400 μL of the growing media to neutralize the 0.25% trypsin-EDTA.
Transfer detached cells into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and spin at 500 × g for 5 min.
Repeat steps a-c.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL PBS.
Add Zombie Red™ Fixable Viability dye at a 1:1000 dilution.
Incubate at RT for 10 min in the dark.
Spin again at 500 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cells in 2% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate at RT for 30 min.
Wash cells with 500 μL PBS to remove residual PFA.
Spin at 500 × g for 5 min.
Repeat step h one more time.
Resuspend the cells in 200 μL PBS.
Infect HEK293-mCAT1 cells with EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP for 24 hours using a 1:100 dilution.
Harvest infected cells as described in the "Analysis by Flow Cytometry" section.
Stain harvested cells with Zombie Red™ Fixable Viability Kit to exclude dead cells.
Analyze stained cells using BD Symphony A3, acquiring 10,000 events.
Resuspend cells in phenol red-free media or PBS for analysis by fluorescence plate reader.
Infect HEK293-mCAT1 cells with EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP for 24 hours.
Harvest the infected cells as described in the "Analysis by Flow Cytometry" section.
Analyze the harvested cells on a fluorescence plate reader (Cytation 5 Cell Imaging Multimode Reader).
Use a fluorescence microscope such as the EVOS cell imaging system or Nikon ECLIPSE Ti2 to measure viral titer based on EGFP-positive cells.
Infect HEK293-mCAT1 cells with EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP for 24 hours.
Harvest the infected cells after 24 hours of infection.
Isolate cellular RNA from harvested cells.
Perform RT-qPCR to detect viral genes inside the HEK293-mCAT1 cells.
Infect HEK293-mCAT1 cells with 10 ng of intact p24 EcoHIV-NDK-EGFP for 24 h.
Wash the infected cells well to remove any unbound viruses.
Isolate RNA from the infected cells according to the "Cellular and viral RNA isolation" protocol.
Use 500 ng RNA for each RT-qPCR reaction.
Calculate copy numbers of gag and spliced vif using standards with known copy numbers (n = 4).
Wash HEK293 cells well as a negative control.
Isolate viral RNA from a 100-fold concentrated aliquot.
Use 1 ng of isolated viral RNA for RT-qPCR reactions as a positive control.
Add 600 μL lysis buffer supplemented with 1% β-mercaptoethanol for each 100 μL of the concentrated viral solution.
Vortex well to lyse the cells.
Pass the lysate 10 times through an 18 G syringe needle to shear DNA.
Add one volume of 70% ethanol to each volume of the cell homogenate.
Vortex to mix and disperse any precipitate.
Transfer 700 μL to the spin cartridge with a collection tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 15 seconds at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through and reinsert the spin cartridge into the same collection tube.
Add 700 μL Wash Buffer I to the spin cartridge.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 15 seconds at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through and place the spin cartridge in a new collection tube.
Add 500 μL Wash Buffer II with ethanol to the spin cartridge.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 15 seconds at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through.
Repeat steps of adding 500 μL Wash Buffer II and centrifuging once more.
Centrifuge the spin cartridge at 12,000 × g for 2 minutes to dry the membrane with bound RNA.
Insert the spin cartridge into a recovery tube.
Add 50 μL RNase-free water to the center of the spin cartridge.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
Centrifuge the spin cartridge for 2 min at 12,000 × g at room temperature to elute RNA from the membrane into the recovery tube.
Measure the RNA concentration with Nanodrop.
Store the purified RNA at -80°C.
Perform RT-qPCR of the isolated RNA using Applied Biosystems™ TaqMan™ Fast Virus 1-Step Master Mix.
In a MicroAmp™ Optical 96-Well Reaction plate, add 5 μL of the Applied Biosystems™ TaqMan™ Fast Virus 1-Step Master Mix.
Add 500 ng of cellular RNA or 1 ng of viral RNA to the reaction plate.
Add 2 μL of the primer/probe mix.
Make the total volume up to 20 μL by adding RNase-free water.
Cover the plate with a MicroAmp™ Optical Adhesive Film.
Centrifuge the plate briefly (∼1 min) to mix the reagents together.
Place the plate in the appropriate qPCR machine.
Set the PCR program as specified for RT-qPCR experiments.
At the end of RT-qPCR experiments, determine the Cycle threshold (Ct) of the reaction to indicate RNA abundance in the sample.
Normalize the Ct values using housekeeping genes such as GAPDH.
Use human GAPDH primers for HEK293-mCAT1 cells and murine GAPDH primers for mice samples.
Reconstitute plasmid standards with known copy numbers.
Quantify intact virus in viral preparations using p24 ELISA.
Determine the amount of free p24 following detergent lysis of viral preparations.
Subtract the amount of free p24 from unlysed samples to measure intact viruses.
Concentrate the supernatant of transfected Lenti-X™ 293T cells at 35,300 × g for 3 hours at 4°C.
Dilute the concentrated virus in 1% Triton™ X-100 and vortex to lyse viral particles.
Alternatively, dilute the concentrated virus with PBS without lysing the viral particles.
Calculate the concentration of free p24 by diluting viral preparations in PBS only.
To calculate total p24 (free and inside viral particles), lyse the viral preparations with assay diluent buffer from the p24 ELISA kit or 1% Triton™ X-100 and vortex.
Inject mice or rats with EcoHIV.
Harvest spleen RNA from infected mice for RT-qPCR analysis.
Isolate spleen RNA from acutely and chronically infected mice.
Use 500 ng of isolated spleen RNA for RT-qPCR reactions.
Isolate the mouse spleen and keep it in 300 μL of RNAlater solution on ice.
Move the spleen into a small dish containing 300 μL cold PBS, using the plunger of sterile 1 mL syringes to release splenocytes gently.
Place a mini-strainer (100 μm) on a 15 mL tube and prime it with 300 μL RNAase-free PBS.
Transfer the splenocytes from step b to the strainer and add 700 μL PBS.
Spin at 500 × g at room temperature for 7 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 5 mL of cold ACK buffer to lyse RBCs.
Keep on ice for 2 min, then spin again as in step e.
Add 600 μL of lysis buffer from the PureLink™ RNA Mini kit to lyse the cell pellet.
Follow steps b-t as described in the cellular and viral RNA isolation section.
Perform RT-qPCR on purified RNA (500 ng) and measure spliced vif, spliced tat, or spliced nef genes.
